baseline.wholesale_association: Four distinct records are associated with NAICS 42 and descendants, including the shared guide and three subsector guides; association is a discovery denominator, not adequacy.
baseline.retail_association: Ten distinct records are associated with NAICS 44-45 and descendants, including the shared guide and seven subsector guides; association is a discovery denominator, not adequacy.

selected_scope.jurisdiction: United States; nongovernmental US GAAP application questions, with state and local tax or unclaimed-property rules separate.
selected_scope.population: Synthetic wholesale merchant, broker or consignor, physical and online retail POS, marketplace settlement and grocery inventory populations at 2026-01-31 with a 2026-02 correction and settlement window.
selected_scope.framework: US GAAP source review using original FASB amendments and current-Codification access boundary; IFRS records remain comparative context and are not substituted for US authority.
selected_scope.period: 2026 reporting date and settlement window; source effective periods are recorded per authority.
selected_scope.industry: NAICS 42 Wholesale Trade and NAICS 44-45 Retail Trade, with Census classification used only to identify business activity and role boundaries.

source_review.status: existing source reused with an additive trade-scoped supplemental review
source_review.effective_period: Original ASU 2014-09 effective dates were deferred by ASU 2015-14; current Topic 606 effective requirements and adoption must be confirmed.
source_review.finding: The issued text supports bounded research on variable consideration, customer payments, returns, customer options, unexercised rights, principal-agent indicators, consignment and bill-and-hold; it is not current consolidated GAAP.
source_review.rights: Publisher terms remain unresolved; no external text is stored.

source_review.locators: Summary pp. 1-5; ASC 606-10-55-36 through 55-40 and related examples; transition 606-10-65-1
source_review.effective_period: Uses Topic 606 adoption and transition dates in the issued update; current effective requirements remain to be confirmed.
source_review.finding: Control of the specified good or service before transfer is the principal-agent starting point; indicators do not replace contract-specific control analysis.
source_review.rights: Publisher terms remain unresolved; no external text is stored.

source_review.locators: Summary pp. 1-3; ASC 330-10-35-1A through 35-1C, printed pp. 4-5
source_review.effective_period: Fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2016, with nonpublic interim and prospective-application details in the update.
source_review.finding: The issued update distinguishes lower-of-cost-and-NRV treatment for methods other than LIFO or retail from the retained LIFO or retail method boundary; it does not establish acquisition cost, ownership or shrinkage posting.
source_review.rights: Publisher terms remain unresolved; no external text is stored.

source_review.effective_period: Specified public entities after fiscal years beginning December 15, 2017; other entities after December 15, 2018, with interim timing stated in the update; earlier application permitted.
source_review.finding: The issued update provides a narrow prepaid stored-value breakage model, with scope exclusions for unclaimed-property remittance, segregated accounts, loyalty programs and other Topics.
source_review.rights: Publisher terms remain unresolved; state unclaimed-property rules and current Topic 405 remain separate.

source_review.finding: Wholesale merchant activity is separated from agents and brokers, and NAICS 425 describes agents or brokers arranging sales of goods owned by others; classification does not decide accounting treatment.
source_review.rights: Census terms and reuse scope remain unresolved; no external text is stored.

question_updates.evidence: US merchant ownership, consignment and custody are separated by specified promise, title, control, physical custody, payment obligation, return rights, shipping or acceptance evidence and inventory risk. A warehouse or dealer confirmation remains an input, not a conclusion.
gaps: Current consolidated ASC 606 and entity contract terms were not accessed.
The package does not determine legal title, shipping terms, acceptance or state-law ownership for a real population.
Dealership and floorplan arrangements remain routed to the separate capital or lending owner.

question_updates.evidence: Merchant, broker and marketplace branches compare price discretion, fulfilment responsibility, inventory and return risk, credit exposure, customer promise and settlement. The same $50,000 customer activity is shown as an agent candidate or principal candidate under mutually exclusive facts.
gaps: No entity marketplace contract, returns clause, guarantee or credit-risk evidence was reviewed.
Gross versus net presentation remains a human conclusion under current consolidated Topic 606.

question_updates.evidence: Customer refunds and return assets, vendor rebates or credits, markdown support, customer payments for distinct services, gift-card liabilities, processor fees and tax are tracked as separate populations. No vendor rebate is netted without contract, earned-status, allocation and current-authority evidence.
gaps: Vendor-consideration and inventory-cost application was not resolved from a current consolidated Topic 330 or entity agreement.
Sales-tax treatment is jurisdiction-specific and excluded.

question_updates.evidence: A proposed read-only workflow freezes transaction, item, location, channel, shipment, delivery, settlement, refund, tender, tax, gift-card, loyalty and inventory populations; joins stable IDs; and reports omissions, duplicates, voids, corrections and in-transit rows separately.
gaps: The fixture is not a live POS, ERP, processor or bank population and does not establish completeness or operating effectiveness.
Settlement agreement does not clear a population or recognition exception by itself.

question_updates.evidence: Wholesale landed-cost arithmetic identifies assumed purchase cost and freight as a cost pool without universal eligibility. Grocery quantity rollforward separates expected ending units, spoilage, counted shrinkage, markdown and supplier-credit questions. US Topic 330 method boundaries remain explicit.
gaps: Current consolidated Topic 330, retail method, LIFO, freight, rebates, shrinkage and perishable-goods policy were not fully reviewed.
A physical count difference is an exception population, not an automatic entry.

question_updates.evidence: The guide distinguishes merchant, reseller, broker, distributor, consignor and marketplace roles, and keeps legal title, control, custody, price-setting, fulfilment, credit risk, returns and commission evidence separate. NAICS 425 supports role classification only.
gaps: No current consolidated Codification access or professional gross-net conclusion was obtained.
Mixed-role contracts can be principal for one promise and agent for another; no live contract population was tested.

AA-I102.gap: Whole-sector and detailed-industry sufficiency remain open.

AA-I102.gap: No operational population or professional workpaper is claimed.

AA-I102.evidence: Assessment gaps retain unresolved current authority, source rights, professional review, empirical support, state tax and floorplan exceptions; counts are explicitly association denominators.
AA-I102.gap: No live control effectiveness or empirical support.

AA-I102.gap: Deployment and cross-account acceptance are not part of this local author check.

AA-I103.gap: Whole-sector and detailed-industry sufficiency remain open.

AA-I103.gap: Current consolidated Codification, state tax and unclaimed-property rules were not reviewed.

AA-I103.evidence: The synthetic fixture reconciles $12,000 card charges to $10,900 deposit, gift-card liability, loyalty population, grocery shrinkage and agent or principal branches.
AA-I103.gap: No live POS, processor or bank population and no posting authority are claimed.

AA-I103.evidence: Retail assessment retains gift-card, loyalty, grocery, marketplace, tax, unclaimed-property, dealership and professional-review limits; no sufficiency is inferred from counts.
AA-I103.gap: No operating effectiveness or empirical retail agent performance.

AA-I103.evidence: The package includes POS, gift-card, grocery and marketplace retrieval fixtures plus generated export and coverage history under the reserved immutable identity.
AA-I103.gap: Deployment and cross-account acceptance are not part of this local author check.

negative_scope: NAICS classifications do not establish control, ownership, recognition or sufficiency.
A net bank deposit does not establish net revenue or an agent role.
Customer returns, vendor rebates, taxes, processor fees, gift-card liabilities, loyalty awards, shrinkage, spoilage and markdowns are not interchangeable offsets.
No universal shrinkage journal, breakage recognition date, vendor-rebate accounting, freight eligibility, sales-tax treatment or unclaimed-property treatment is asserted.

Dealership and floorplan lending, state or local law, real contracts, current consolidated Codification access, professional sign-off, production validation and empirical agent performance remain outside this package.
